Standard accessors for a stochastic frontier model

Source: R/methods.sfmodel.R
sfmodel-methods.Rd

The methods that R's modelling conventions lead a user to reach for. Without them coef() falls through to coef.default(), which looks for an element named coefficients, finds none, and returns NULL rather than saying so.

# S3 method for class 'sfmodel'
coef(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sfmodel'
vcov(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sfmodel'
nobs(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sfmodel'
fitted(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sfmodel'
residuals(object, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sfmodel'
predict(object, newdata = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'sfmodel'
logLik(object, ...)

Arguments

object

an object of class "sfmodel" carrying posterior draws.

...

further arguments, unused.

newdata

an optional data frame in which to look for the variables of the frontier. If omitted, the data the model was built on are used.

Value

coef() a named vector of posterior means of the frontier coefficients; vcov() their posterior covariance matrix; nobs() the number of observations; fitted() and predict() the frontier; residuals() the composed error; and logLik() the log-likelihood at the posterior mean, with the attributes that AIC and BIC need.

Details

A frontier model has two natural notions of a fitted value, and they are kept apart here. fitted() returns the frontier, the maximum output the inputs allow, which is what the coefficients describe, including any offset. residuals() returns the composed error, which still contains the one-sided term and is therefore not centred on zero. Use efficiency for the inefficiency part of it. The two are related as usual: the residual is the response as supplied minus the fitted frontier, whether or not there is an offset.

Every one of these summarises the posterior by its mean. That is a convenience, not the object: the draws themselves are in object$posterior, and summary.sfmodel reports their spread.

See also

summary.sfmodel for the posterior summaries, efficiency for the scores, selection_criteria for the criteria in the form the package reports them.

Examples

set.seed(1234)
d <- sim_sf(n = 200, beta = c(1, 0.5, 0.3), sigma_v = 0.2, par_u = 4)

model <- create_sfmodel_exp(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d,
                            iterations = 500, burnin = 200)
model <- add_posterior_coefficients(add_priors(model))

coef(model)
#> (Intercept)          x1          x2 
#>   0.9920230   0.5017208   0.3111385 
nobs(model)
#> [1] 200
head(residuals(model))
#>           1           2           3           4           5           6 
#> -0.80709665 -0.40167082 -0.16104939  0.03973322 -0.48266937 -0.13998675 
AIC(model)
#> [1] 82.50257
